investigation: Octupole Deformation and Triaxial Chiral Geometry Coupling across Mass Regions
description: Systematic 3D-TAC evaluation of the competition between triaxial aplanar rotation and reflection-asymmetric octupole deformation, establishing the critical octupole threshold beta3_crit driving chiral quenching and planar restoration.

systems.structure_regime: Planar Magnetic Rotation (Shears Band Crossing, PRC 2014)

boundary_1_octupole_axialization_chiral_.contrast: 78Br (chiral quadruplet, beta3=0.045) vs 224Ra (static pear rotor, beta3=0.140)
boundary_1_octupole_axialization_chiral_.mechanism: In 78Br, the octupole degree of freedom is a dynamic vibration around a triaxial minimum (gamma = 26 deg). Because beta3 (0.045) is small compared to beta3_crit (0.125), the octupole phonon couples with the aplanar rotation (phi_0 = 41.2 deg) to double the chiral doublet into a D2 x P*T chiral-octupole quadruplet. In 224Ra, large static octupole deformation (beta3 = 0.140) exerts an overwhelming dipole-octupole restoring torque that aligns all multipole vectors along the intrinsic symmetry axis, flattening triaxiality (gamma -> 0) and crushing the out-of-plane angle phi_0 -> 0 deg, completely extinguishing chirality.
boundary_1_octupole_axialization_chiral_.failure_signature: Predicting chiral doublets or quadruplets in nuclei with strong static octupole deformation.

boundary_2_planar_magnetic_rotation_rest.mechanism: In 198Bi, small quadrupole deformation (beta2 = 0.10) and near-axial geometry (gamma = 10 deg) reduce triaxiality, while the massive multiquasiparticle neutron blade (j_nu = 16.5 hbar) provides an overwhelming in-plane Coriolis restoring force, suppressing the chiral out-of-plane angle to 0 deg and locking the system into planar magnetic rotation.
boundary_2_planar_magnetic_rotation_rest.failure_signature: Confusing multi-band magnetic rotation crossings with chiral-octupole quadruplets.
